Evidence of a hazardous second-hand market has been presented by the market surveillance support service (Division responsibilities for pharmaceuticals (EYK): B-3303–2023(EYDIR) and B-5202–2023(EYDIR)) as well as the market surveillance support service (Division Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices), which is responsible for the assessment and application of technical regulations covering electronic products. The market surveillance support service, the department for market and consumer protection provides experts to evaluate the market and to provide back up in cases of violations.This project was conducted from December 9th to December 10th and December 11th, 2023 at the RZH-Research Institute for Hygiene in Männedorf, where the market surveillance initiative "Market surveillance on electronic products" started in the EYF group, which belonged to the EYC group ( Environment, Energy, Consumers and Welfare). The market surveillance service aims to identify product violations and the implications of violations. Our principal objectives within this Framework for market and consumer protection are as follows: To develop a framework for legislation which aims to minimise the risk of misuse of electronic products (digital services, smart), make it easier for Finnish users of these products to perform their assessments and to "tune" the products, to compensate for adverse effects on consumers in the electronic field which are a result of the uses/use of these products.The main objectives of our market surveillance initiative "Market surveillance on electronic products" are: To develop and support the framework of technical regulations. (e.g. suitable classifications of products, labelling, coverage) to minimise the risks associated with misuse of electronic products such as digital services, smart, and specify the consequences of misuse of the products. Furthermore, to ensure the usefulness of electronic products and their use in order to provide the necessary awareness and knowledge of users and their dependence thereon, so that risks associated with these products can be minimised.These objectives can be concretized as follows: - To identify problems with electronics of uncertain impact or misuse of specific electronic products, which can reduce the requirements in the existing legislation. (e.g. labelling, cover), which are already applicable, but which are rather unfavourable pieces of legislation) - to provide knowledge about the possible side effects and consequences of use of specific electronic products. (e.g. due to design of electronic devices - electronic consumer advice, electromagnetic emissions, radiation hazards), and the respective precautions. They also include a list of chemicals that cause such problems, regardless of the use of the product, examples of products and evaluations within the context of these clauses - to ensure a holistic risk assessment in order to take appropriate measures in connection with product-use, taking into account possible restrictions, (e.g. labelling, etc.), guidelines and information. (For example, allergens in organic compounds, caffeine, etc.). **Part 5-22: Installation of fieldbuses – Installation profiles for CPF 22**

**1 Scope**

This part of IEC 61784-5 specifies the installation profile for CPF 22 (AUTBUS™ 1).

The installation profile is specified in Annex A. This annex is read in conjunction with IEC 61918:2018, IEC 61918:2018/AMD1:2022 and IEC 61918:2018/AMD2:2024.

**2 Normative references**

The following documents are referred to in the text in such a way that some or all of their content constitutes requirements of this document. For dated references, only the edition cited applies. For undated references, the latest edition of the referenced document (including any amendments) applies.

IEC 61918:2018[2], *Industrial communication networks – Installation of communication networks in industrial premises*
IEC 61918:2018/AMD1:2022
IEC 61918:2018/AMD2:2024

NOTE For profile specific normative references, see Clause A.2.

**3 Terms, definitions and abbreviated terms**

For the purposes of this document, the terms, definitions and abbreviated terms given in IEC 61918:2018, Clause 3 and IEC 61918:2018/AMD1:2022, Clause 3, apply.

ISO and IEC maintain terminology databases for use in standardization at the following addresses:

- IEC Electropedia: available at [https://www.electropedia.org/](https://www.electropedia.org/)
- ISO Online browsing platform: available at [https://www.iso.org/obp](https://www.iso.org/obp)

**4 CPF 22: Overview of installation profiles**

CPF 22 consists of one communication profile as specified in IEC 61784-1:2023.

The installation requirements for CP 22/1 (AUTBUS™) are specified in Annex A.

6 Conformance to installation profiles

Each installation profile within this document includes part of the IEC 61698-4-2 duties, amendments, additions or information and any corresponding subdivisions, additions or information used in accordance with their degree of conformity or performance and, where appropriate, reference to the applicable subclauses or subclauses. It may also include defined additional specifications.

A statement of compliance with an installation profile of this document shall be stated as either Compliance with IEC 61698-4-2 duties, amendments, additions or information and any modifications, additions or information, or Compliance with IEC 61698-4-2 duties, amendments, additions or information and any corrections or renovations.

##### 103. Character States
So far, we have performed comparisons between literals using the `equals` method and literals using character
sets. This introduces some inaccuracies during programmming, such as directly accepting the timestamp
''+'' at a fixed place in a byte array with distinct size, leading to possible object reset. To mitigate this
issue, a method named `decodeect` was provided to safely convert strings and byte arrays.
    - If the `length` of the input is approximately equal to the length of the resulting byte array, an error message is pre-interpreted, or a single character is discarded from the in-stream.
    - When the `length` of the input is obviously not a multiple of the byte number, the remaining `length` represents zeros.

When working on character data types, the minimum size must be considered unless a library provides a more precise
interface. This jest can be utilized to predict the proper fitment size. In Python, if all overflow will never happen
, then it can be avoided to assume "(...) max(long Ortega 5-22-2024 c)"".
##### 104. Missing Values
Unfortunately, when in-stream data is not available, invalid data values could not be accepted. The specific problem is that `invalid characters` cannot be identified by the script while deduplication is being performed. Therefore, invalid data values (data retention method) must be ignored during deduplication. In addition, the node does not provide `Create and Get Operation` and thus does not allow modification and retrieving of the stored values. To solve these problems, the `custom log format` can be used, named `custom log fixed-size transpose`, in which a specific element in the log is replaced with a `fixed size`. This specific element is used later for redundant processing of invalid values, such as missing value.
Based on the `invalid data values` reported in the testsnake-overlap, there are more cases where single-hot-encoded numeric values are required to support `.api/breadcrumbs`. Since node only keeps the format of `width-height`, using a header of `width-height` implicitly converts space characters (`) into shape characters (`), comprising `empty cell``, ensure tile copies, and handle counting cells. Other than `is disabled(c bool, bool)`, no special check for pass-through is executed. So far, no specific algorithms have been designed as a special case to resolving this issue.

outdoor zone of a building where temperature fluctuations are strong but that also includes the courtyard. It is characterized by a very common design feature: a double wall between the inside and the outside. An analysis of the incidences indicated that the main failings were related to the construction and the poor construction of the double wall, rolled doors and roll bars that do not achieve a tight door fit or draw when the doors are closed.

The main failings in both cases are related to the damage made to the specimen left open to the elements. The results allowed to notice the use of high-quality raw materials, common with exposed construction, and the absence of any prevention measures or reinforcement of the wall.All the elements specified in the previous items were followed by the risk of damage from the exposure to the environment due to water acidity. Water levels should be in a range of 60-120, while the pH should be around 5.5-7.5. Temperature levels are between 0 and 35º and relative humidity between 40 and 80%.To conclude, the main findings of the tests carried out show a high vulnerability of the construction of the double wall of the building. This vulnerable building is the result of poorly jointed and riveted components, not executed with a proper plan for the prevention of the flow of water.It is suggested that an urgent investigation be carried out to evaluate the state of conservation and degradation of the components through visual reviews, scanning, and cathodic tests. In case of need, repair and reinforcement works for the most damaged elements should be undertaken.The prevention and waterproofing works should be carried out in the case of a realization contract with an accredited building survey or a control office.

A few elements that have not yet been financed for estimation are the solar gain on the walls, the entrance and around the outside door, the mobilization of the existing windows (assuming a maintenance window), and the anti-summation of the apartments.

References
1. Manual of Computerized Procedures for Track II: Thermal Calculations, National Buildings Code Institute, Ottawa (can be found at https://blackmarble.org/104_241.pdf, date: 2020-10-17).

2. Manual of the Building Construction Code, Part A – 2020, Federal Justice Council – National Industry – Environmental Service, Ministry of Justice (can be found at https://www.utsa.ca/files/retitle/internal_transportation_CCI.PDF, date: 2020-10-15).

3. Circular CNC C60: Standard technique for thermal transmittance of building construction and conversion, National Building Code, Ottawa, (can be found in corp.Lib. et閱集可卷，27-8-2023，ISSN非：0-982-8892/AJ，date: 2024-04-2023).

4. PP PM RTPF 50 S (confirmed its detection and confirmed that it does not meet the requirements for this kind of building)

**1. La Commission Électrotechnique Internationale (IEC) est une organisation mondiale de normalisation composée de l'ensemble des comités électrotechniques nationaux (Comités nationaux de l'IEC). L'IEC a pour objet de favoriser et coopérer dans la lutte contre les défis du numérique, avec une orientation en la matière de la sécurité, de l'échange, des Sensibilités, de l'équité, de l'éthique ainsi que des Tâches publiques.**
**2. Les décisions ou accords officiels de l'IEC concernant les questions techniques représentent, dans la mesure du possible, un accord international sur les sujets étudiés, étant donné que les Comités nationaux de l'IECintéressés sont représentés dans chaque comité d'études.**
**3. Les Publications de l'IEC se présentent sous la forme de recommandations internationales et sont agréées comme telles par les Comités nationaux de l'IEC. Tous les efforts raisonnables sont entrepris afin que l'IEC s'assure de l'exactitude du contenu technique de ses publications; l'IEC ne peut pas être tenue responsable de l'éventuelle mauvaise utilisation ou interprétation qui en est faite par un quelconque utilisateur final.**
**4. Dans le but d'encourager l'uniformité internationale, les Comités nationaux de l'IEC s'engagent, dans toute la mesure possible, à appliquer de façon transparente les Publications de l'IEC dans leurs publications nationales et régionales. Toutes divergences entre toutes Publications de l'IEC et toutes publications nationales ou régionales correspondantes doivent être indiquées en termes clairs dans ces dernières.**
**5. L'IEC elle-même ne fournit aucune attestation de conformité. Des organismes de certification indépendants fournissent des services d'évaluation de conformité et, dans certains secteurs, accèdent aux marques de conformité de l'IEC. L'IEC n'est responsable d'aucun des services effectués par les organismes de certification indépendants.**
**6. Tous les utilisateurs doivent s'assurer qu'ils sont en possession de la dernière édition de cette publication.**
**7. Aucune responsabilité ne doit être imputée à l'IEC, à ses administrateurs, employés, auxiliaires ou mandataires, y compris ses experts particuliers et les membres de ses comités d'études et des Comités nationaux de l'IEC, pour tout préjudice causé en cas de dommages corporels et matériels, ou de tout autre dommage de quelque nature que ce soit, directe ou indirecte, ou pour supporter les coûts (y compris les frais de justice) et les dépenses découlant de la publication ou de l'utilisation de cette Publication de l'IEC ou de toute autre Publication de l'IEC, ou au crédit qui lui est accordé.**
**8. L'attention est attirée sur les références normatives citées dans cette publication. L'utilisation de publications référencées est obligatoire pour une application correcte de la présente publication.**
**9. L'IEC attire l'attention sur le fait que la mise en application du présent document peut entraîner l'utilisation d'un ou de plusieurs brevets. L'IEC ne prend pas position quant à la preuve, à la validité et à l'applicabilité de tout droit de propriété revendiqué à cet égard. **6 Conformité aux profils d’installation**

supplémentaires.

comme suit:

Conformité à l’IEC 61784-5-22:2024 pour CP 22/m <nom> ou

Conformité à l’IEC 61784-5-22 (Éd.1) pour CP 22/m <nom>.

Le nom indiqué entre crochets obliques < > est facultatif et les crochets obliques ne doivent
pas être inclus. Le "m" dans CP 22/m doit être remplacé par le numéro de profil 1.

NOTE Le nom peut être celui du profil, par exemple AUTBUS.

Si le nom est une appellation commerciale, l’autorisation du détenteur de l’appellation
commerciale doit être exigée.

informatifs, autres que les dispositions d’essai du produit (évaluation et examen).
